children: Colombia's consumer prices rose 0.37% in September, the country's DANE statistics agency said on Wednesday, taking annual price growth to 6.29%.
The September figure was below the 0.40% median forecast of analysts polled by Reuters, and lower than the 0.39% recorded in August.
Annual inflation edged up from 6.24% in August but came in below the 6.32% forecast by analysts.
Inflation remains well above the central bank's target of 3% plus or minus one percentage point.
The monthly increases were led by food and non-alcoholic beverages, housing, water, electricity, gas and other fuels, and education.
Latin America's fourth-largest economy is facing deteriorating fiscal accounts due to declining revenues and rising spending.
A large part of southwestern and central Colombia was hit by the powerful August 10 quake, which killed 335 people, injured thousands more and destroyed homes and infrastructure.
Reconstruction is expected to cost at least 30 trillion Colombian pesos ($9.29 billion) according to government estimates.
